{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative bias (e.g., -0.25 or 0.00) and true prices show strong downward momentum.",
    "Reduce forecast overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70.00) by applying a 5-10% downward correction to prevent overreaction.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 10-15% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices (last 3-5 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative — especially if true price has recently fallen below forecast.",
    "For horizon >15 days, reduce forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average of past 30d true values, especially if sentiment is flat or negative.",
    "If true price drops below 65.00 after a spike, assume downward momentum and reduce forecast by 5-10% for next 3 days unless sentiment turns bullish.",
    "When sentiment history includes 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days, assume low volatility and adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day true average."
  ]
}
